verdict.rationale: cubic documents several autonomous, event-triggered behaviors that users can switch on. It automatically reviews every new PR, can auto-fix issues from every review, can auto-approve low-risk PRs, can auto-resolve threads, and can automatically check PRs against linked issues. Fixes are described as running in the background. These are fixed toggles tied to the PR lifecycle, not a general builder for user-defined automations or recurring schedules. Missing for 10: user-defined or custom automation workflows, recurring/scheduled runs (e.g., scheduled codebase scans), and independent hands-on corroboration of the background runs.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can set up automations that run autonomously in the background

citations.quote: Once installed, cubic automatically reviews new pull requests.
turn on auto-fix to have cubic fix the issues from every review of a pull request.
Auto-approval lets you skip human review for pull requests that cubic determines are low risk and issue-free.
Enable automatic thread resolution to close findings when the issue is fixed
cubic can automatically fix issues in the background.
cubic can automatically analyze your pull requests to see if they meet the requirements from your linked Linear, Jira, Asana, or GitHub issues.
